assets.description: Customer personal data (name, email, address) stored in the database.
Customer credit card data stored in the database.
Payment API that processes financial transactions.

vulnerabilities.description: Login form is susceptible to SQL injection, allowing attackers to bypass authentication or extract customer personal data.

nist.justification: Enforcing strict input validation and parameterized queries directly prevents SQL injection by ensuring malicious input is never interpreted as executable SQL code.

vulnerabilities.description: Credit card data is stored without adequate encryption, exposing it in cleartext if the database is compromised.

nist.justification: SC-28 directly mandates cryptographic protection of sensitive data stored at rest, ensuring that credit card data is encrypted and unreadable even if the database is compromised.

vulnerabilities.description: No rate limiting on the login endpoint allows unlimited authentication attempts, enabling brute-force attacks against customer accounts.

nist.justification: AC-7 explicitly requires limiting and responding to consecutive failed authentication attempts, directly mitigating brute-force attacks by locking out or throttling repeated login failures.

vulnerabilities.description: The payment API lacks proper authorization checks, potentially allowing one customer to trigger or view transactions belonging to another.

nist.justification: AC-3 requires enforcement of approved authorizations for access to system resources, ensuring that the payment API validates that each customer can only access their own transactions.

vulnerabilities.description: Sensitive credit card data is transmitted to the payment API over an unencrypted channel, exposing it to interception.

nist.justification: SC-8 mandates cryptographic protection of data in transit, directly preventing interception of sensitive credit card data transmitted between the client and the payment API.

vulnerabilities.description: Detailed error messages from the database or payment API are exposed to end users, leaking system internals and sensitive data.

nist.justification: SI-11 directly requires that systems generate error messages revealing only information necessary for corrective action and not expose sensitive internals, eliminating the information leakage from verbose error messages.

threats.description: An external attacker exploits SQL injection on the login form to dump the customer database, extracting personal data and credit card records.
threats.likelihood_justif: SQL injection on login forms is extremely common and widely automated, but modern frameworks and WAFs reduce success rates significantly; still plausible if input validation is weak.

threats.description: An external attacker performs a brute-force credential stuffing attack against the login endpoint to take over customer accounts.
threats.likelihood_justif: Credential stuffing is fully automated, requires no special skill, and is one of the most frequently observed attacks against any internet-facing login endpoint today.

threats.description: An external attacker intercepts network traffic between the shop and the payment API to capture credit card data in transit.
threats.likelihood_justif: TLS is universally adopted for payment API communications, making in-transit interception extremely difficult without prior compromise of an endpoint, making this scenario very rare in practice.

threats.description: An authenticated malicious customer manipulates payment API requests to access or alter another customer's transactions via an IDOR vulnerability.
threats.likelihood_justif: IDOR vulnerabilities in payment flows are commonly discovered by opportunistic attackers and security researchers; exploiting them requires only a valid authenticated session and basic request manipulation.

threats.description: A malicious insider with database access extracts stored cleartext credit card data for financial gain.
threats.likelihood_justif: Storing cleartext credit card data violates PCI-DSS and is increasingly rare; while insider threats are real, the combination of direct DB access and unencrypted card data being present simultaneously is uncommon in modern systems.

scenarios.vuln_desc: Login form is susceptible to SQL injection, allowing attackers to bypass authentication or extract customer personal data.
scenarios.impact_justif: SQL injection enabling full database dump exposes mass personal data and payment records, constituting a catastrophic confidentiality breach with severe regulatory consequences.

scenarios.threat_desc: An external attacker exploits SQL injection on the login form to dump the customer database, extracting personal data and credit card records.

scenarios.impact_justif: Verbose error messages leak system internals and potentially partial sensitive data, aiding attackers but not directly causing mass data exposure on their own.

scenarios.threat_desc: An external attacker performs a brute-force credential stuffing attack against the login endpoint to take over customer accounts.

scenarios.impact_justif: Successful credential stuffing leads to bulk customer account takeover, exposing personal data and enabling fraudulent transactions across many accounts.

scenarios.impact_justif: Unencrypted transmission of credit card data to the payment API allows interception of live payment credentials in cleartext, causing catastrophic confidentiality and PCI-DSS compliance failure.

scenarios.threat_desc: An authenticated malicious customer manipulates payment API requests to access or alter another customer's transactions via an IDOR vulnerability.

scenarios.impact_justif: IDOR exploitation allowing modification or viewing of other customers' transactions directly compromises transaction integrity and financial data confidentiality at scale.

scenarios.impact_justif: A malicious insider extracting cleartext credit card records results in deliberate, targeted mass disclosure of highly regulated financial data with direct fraud potential.
